messages:
amal: Heads up — nightly perf run shows a big p95 regression after merge r2467, canary slowed from ~120ms -> ~310ms. Rollout paused. :warning:
ci-bot: CI perf alert: build r2467 failed perf gate. p50 70ms -> 180ms, p95 120ms -> 310ms (+158%). Report: https://ci.redwood/incoming/2467
devon: Yikes. PR #2467 touched kernel selection ordering + a tiny KV pack tweak. Could be an interaction.
mira: I can reproduce locally on my devbox, using the perf harness. Quick repro I used:
```
git checkout abc1234   # merge r2467 tip
./scripts/perf_run.sh --model gpt-small --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --runs 30
# collects p50/p95, prints JSON to out/perf.json
```
Result: p95 ~310ms consistently.
tera: Same here on a single 3090 dev machine — p95 ~300ms. I captured a flamegraph; there's an extra memcpy during KV restore and more time in kernel selection path.
devon: Can we do a two-point confirm? checkout parent commit and compare numbers (no bench noise):
```
# parent commit
git checkout def5678
./scripts/perf_run.sh --model gpt-small --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --runs 30
# then tip
git checkout abc1234
./scripts/perf_run.sh --model gpt-small --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --runs 30
```
I ran this: def5678 -> p95 118ms, abc1234 -> p95 310ms. Repro is solid.
mira: I inspected the commit window: `git log --oneline def5678..abc1234` shows (newest->oldest):
- a4d2f1 adjust kernel selection orders
- b7f4e3 kv-pack eviction tweak
- 9c1e2a small batching heuristic tweak
My hunch: kernel-order change interacts badly with kv-pack (b7f4e3) so both present cause slowdown.
tera: The flamegraph shows kernel selection doing extra candidate checks leading to fallback to a slower kernel path which triggers slab copies when restoring KV. That amplifies with batching.
devon: Quick experiment: force the old kernel selection on the regression tip: `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy ./serve --perf-mode` — when I do that on abc1234, p95 drops to ~125ms. So kernel reorder is the immediate trigger.
amal: Great catch. So root cause = interaction between kernel-order change (a4d2f1) and kv-pack tweaks (b7f4e3). Fix options: revert a4d2f1, or add guards so the new selection is not used when KV pack mode enabled. Revert is fastest to unblock rollout.
tera: I'll draft a focused revert for a4d2f1 (only kernel-order logic) and push a small test exercising the kernel decision matrix to prevent regressions.
ci-bot: Note: any revert must run the perf gate job (it currently flaps). Suggest we open a revert PR and mark it for `perf-critical` tag.
devon: Opening PR now: branch `revert/kernel-order-2472`, PR #2472. I pushed a commit that reverts a4d2f1 and adds a unit test for selection fallback. Local perf on that branch: p95 122ms (stable).
mira: I validated #2472 on my machine and on a small canary node — perf aligns with parent. I endorse merging to canary.
amal: Plan: merge revert PR to canary, run overnight perf harness and new CI perf job. If stable, roll forward to main and resume rollout. Follow-up: create an instrumented experiment to safely re-apply kernel-order optimization later with a KV-packed compatibility flag.
tera: I'll also add a short-term canary config to force legacy kernel selection for customers on the canary pool so we don't regress live traffic while we validate.
ci-bot: Canary update will be gated until PR #2472 passes perf gate. CI queue updated.
amal: Thanks all. Great coordinated narrowing — saved the rollout. Please paste perf job links here after CI finishes so we can close the incident. :thumbsup:
